body.text: The PRA is the plant model that provides an integrated assessment of risk to the public.
body.anchor: is the plant model that provides an integrated assessment of risk to the public

body.text: The NEI 18-04 methodology, endorsed by RG 1.233, is implemented without deviation for LBE selection and evaluation.
body.anchor: is implemented without deviation for licensing basis event (LBE) selection and evaluation

body.text: LBE selection includes the systematic definition, categorization, and evaluation of event sequences.
body.anchor: The selection of LBEs includes the systematic definition, categorization, and evaluation of event sequences

body.text: Radionuclide sources in the PRA include the RES, SPS and SCG, gaseous radwaste, the EVHM, the EVST, spent fuel processing, and the Spent Fuel Pool.
body.anchor: The following sources of radionuclides are evaluated by the PRA

body.text: At the construction permit stage, the PRA is internal events at-power and low-power shutdown only.
body.anchor: internal events at-power and low-power shutdown only

checks.q: What methodology is used for LBE selection and evaluation?
checks.x: NEI 18-04, as endorsed by RG 1.233, is implemented without deviation.
checks.anchor: is implemented without deviation for licensing basis event (LBE) selection and evaluation

body.text: BDBEs are event sequences with mean frequencies of 5x10^-7 to 1x10^-4 per plant-year.
body.anchor: Event sequences with mean frequencies of 5x10-7 per plant-year to 1x10-4 per plant-year are classified as BDBEs

body.text: The DBE frequency ceiling used in the DID evaluation is 1x10^-2 per plant-year, and the BDBE ceiling is 1x10^-4.
body.anchor: The frequency of all DBEs and BDBEs

body.text: Tables 3.5-1, 3.5-2, and 3.5-3 summarize the AOOs, DBEs, and BDBEs. Table 3.5-4 maps DBEs to DBAs and gives each DBA's dose consequence.
body.anchor: The table provides a mapping of DBEs to DBAs

checks.q: A sequence with a mean frequency of 1x10^-5 per plant-year is classified as what?
checks.x: Mean frequencies of 5x10^-7 to 1x10^-4 per plant-year are classified as BDBEs.
checks.anchor: Event sequences with mean frequencies of 5x10-7 per plant-year to 1x10-4 per plant-year are classified as BDBEs

body.text: Bounding parameters are selected for DBAs.
body.anchor: Bounding parameters are selected for use in evaluating design basis accidents

body.text: DBA analyses consider only safety-related SSCs for mitigation. AOO, DBE, and BDBE analyses take into account the expected response of all SSCs, regardless of safety classification.
body.anchor: AOO, DBE, and BDBE analyses take into account the expected response of all SSCs

body.text: AOO, DBE, and BDBE transients use either the conservative DBA approach or a best-estimate plus uncertainty approach.
The assumption that a function fails in an LBE description does not necessarily mean the failure resulted from the initiating event.
body.anchor: does not necessarily mean the failure was a result of the LBE initiating event

checks.q: Which SSCs are considered for mitigation in DBA analyses?
checks.x: Only safety-related SSCs are considered for mitigation in DBA analyses.
checks.anchor: Where only safety-related SSCs are considered for

body.text: LBEs with releases are evaluated for 30 days.
body.anchor: LBEs with releases are evaluated for 30 days

cells: Peak cladding temperature below 1157 F (625 C) and stable or decreasing, with K-effective 1.0 (BDBE only) or less and core power stable or reducing
Used if there is no scram. K-effective 1.0, with heat removal equal to heat production
rows.anchor: Heat removal is equal to heat production

body.text: Transients that rely on passive long-term cooling must also show heat removal exceeds total heat produced.
body.anchor: Heat removal exceeds total heat produced

checks.q: What peak cladding temperature limit defines the safe shutdown end state?
checks.x: The safe shutdown state requires peak cladding temperature below 1157 F (625 C), stable or decreasing.

checks.q: What full power core inlet temperature is assumed in the LBE analyses?
checks.x: Full power assumes 100% power, 100% flow, and 360.1 C core inlet.

body.text: LBEs are risk-significant if the site boundary dose exceeds 2.5 mrem over 30 days and the frequency of the dose is within one percent of the F-C target.
body.anchor: LBEs are classified as risk-significant if the LBE site boundary dose exceeds 2.5 mrem over 30 days

body.text: BDBEs are high-consequence if the dose exceeds 10 CFR 50.34 criteria.
body.anchor: BDBEs are classified as high-consequence if the dose exceeds 10 CFR 50.34 criteria

body.alt: PSAR Rev 1 figure: F-C Chart for LBEs with Uncertainty Bands

checks.q: When is a BDBE classified as high-consequence?
o: When the dose exceeds 10 CFR 50.34 criteria
checks.x: BDBEs are high-consequence if the dose exceeds 10 CFR 50.34 criteria.
checks.anchor: BDBEs are classified as high-consequence if the dose exceeds 10 CFR 50.34 criteria

checks.q: What is the target for EAB early fatality risk?
checks.x: The EAB early fatality metric target is 5x10^-7 per plant-year.
checks.anchor: early fatality integrated risk metric target of 5×10-7 per plant-year

body.text: The major accident is a deterministic analysis that meets 10 CFR 50.34(a)(1)(ii)(D).
body.anchor: The Major Accident is a deterministic analysis that meets the requirement of 10 CFR 50.34(a)(1)(ii)(D)

body.text: For Kemmerer Unit 1, the EAB and LPZ are the same boundary, a 0.25-mile radius from the Reactor Building centerpoint.
body.anchor: the Exclusion Area Boundary (EAB) and Low Population Zone (LPZ) are the same boundary

body.text: The DBA with the maximum core damage and associated in-vessel release was selected as the major accident.
body.anchor: The DBA with the maximum core damage and associated in-vessel release

checks.q: What radius defines both the EAB and LPZ for Kemmerer Unit 1?
checks.x: The EAB and LPZ are the same boundary at a 0.25-mile radius.
checks.anchor: the Exclusion Area Boundary (EAB) and Low Population Zone (LPZ) are the same boundary

title: Licensing Basis Events
subject: licensing basis events
intro: The PSAR uses a risk-informed framework. This lesson explains how events are found, sorted by frequency, analyzed, and judged.

objectives.text: Describe the role of the PRA in selecting licensing basis events.
Classify AOOs, DBEs, and BDBEs by frequency, and describe DBAs.
Explain how analysis assumptions differ between DBAs and other LBEs.
State the initial conditions and end states used in LBE analysis.
Explain what makes an LBE risk-significant or a BDBE high-consequence.
State the three cumulative risk metrics.
